title: PhD / Doctoral Research
summary: Three to four years of doctoral research with a Chinese supervisor, built around a research proposal that fits the lab and the funding.
overview: A Chinese PhD is a research appointment as much as a degree. The supervisor, lab and publication record matter more than the university's general reputation. English-taught doctoral programs exist in science, engineering, medicine and some social sciences.

The application is a research proposal, academic CV, references and a supervisor who agrees to take you. Funding can come from a university scholarship, a provincial program or CSC. We help you identify realistic supervisors, prepare the proposal and understand what the funding actually covers.
fitFor: You hold a master's degree or an equivalent research qualification
You have a research direction and preferably publications
You want a supervisor and lab, not just a university name
You are applying for a funded or partially funded doctorate
outcomes: A doctoral degree from a Chinese university
Access to Chinese laboratories and research networks
A foundation for an academic or industry research career

timeline.text: We define the research area, map supervisors and check their recent publications and intake capacity.
Research proposal, academic CV, references and language evidence are prepared; supervisor contact begins.
University and CSC applications are submitted; interviews and academic reviews are prepared.
Offer, funding confirmation, JW202, visa and arrival. Lab and housing arrangements are confirmed.

faq.question: Can I do a PhD in English in China?
faq.answer: Yes, at many universities in science, engineering, medicine and some social sciences. The supervisor's working language matters more than the official program label, so we confirm it directly.

faq.question: Is a supervisor's acceptance enough for admission?
faq.answer: Not always. Most universities still require a formal application, academic review and sometimes an interview. A supervisor's support is important but does not replace the university's process.
